context_documents.body:
# 2023-930: A borrowed belt gripper needs its operating clearance, not just its layout

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The polyurethane-belt gripper credits WildStang’s published work. Stand-offs keep running belts away from the carpet. A continuously rigged, internally belted elevator leaves an open arm passage; an auxiliary cube collector is discussed as a later low/link opportunity.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team cites grip on cones, carpet protection and keeping elevator gearing/mass low. The auxiliary collector must remain a proposal unless its later fielded configuration is established.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Copying the contact belt without its stand-offs can create both carpet damage and an unintended ground reaction on the arm. A low-mounted drive reduces moving mass, while an open passage permits acquisition on the opposite side. The strategic value of an added cube collector depends on finishing links quickly, not simply acquiring another mechanism.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test floor clearance under chassis pitch, compare both piece types, and measure complete low-node cycles before adding the proposed subsystem.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
